basis: Neurologic impairment, hearing loss and retinal degeneration each commonly exceed 30%; hepatic disease also qualifies but is omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.hepatic: none: common hepatic involvement is omitted at the four-axis cap; neurologic and sensory dysfunction are retained across the PEX26 spectrum.
decisions.ocular: involved: retinal degeneration with visual impairment commonly exceeds 30% across the Zellweger spectrum.

basis: Hindbrain malformation with an occipital or high cervical encephalocele through a defining skull or vertebral defect.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the occipital or upper cervical bony defect containing the encephalocele is a defining structural component of Chiari III.

basis: Sympathetic pathway damage causes miosis, mild ptosis and anhidrosis; these signs generally preserve vision and do not establish additional eye or skin damage.

decisions.ocular: none: miosis and mild ptosis are signs of sympathetic denervation, generally without impaired vision or intrinsic ocular damage.

basis: Renal insufficiency 5/5; neurodevelopmental impairment in most and hearing loss ~70-90%. Respiratory failure need not reflect intrinsic lung injury; myopathy omitted at cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: neurodevelopmental impairment and structural CNS abnormalities affect most patients; the defining disorder is mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation deficiency.

basis: Defined by malignant occupation of nipple epidermis with persistent skin injury; breast origin does not negate the defining epidermal disease.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: malignant Paget cells occupy the nipple epidermis, producing defining chronic skin lesions; this is demonstrable skin disease despite mammary origin.

basis: MELAS defines mitochondrial encephalomyopathy and lactic acidosis; sensorineural hearing loss affects ~40-60% of MELAS patients, with uncertain MT-ND1-specific frequency.

decisions.otologic: involved: hearing loss affects ~40-60% in MELAS; the parent syndrome supports inclusion, although the MT-ND1-specific frequency is uncertain.

basis: Autoinflammatory dermatosis with inflammatory subcutaneous fat loss; myositis, muscle wasting and fixed contractures commonly affect at least ~30%.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: inflammatory loss of subcutaneous fat supports dermatologic disease; lipodystrophy alone does not establish a common metabolic or endocrine disorder.

basis: Cranioskeletal and ectodermal dysplasia includes defining dental defects (2/2); progressive renal disease affects ~50-80% of CED. Ocular defects (1/2) omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: involved: progressive renal tubulopathy is a common complication, approximately 50-80% across cranioectodermal dysplasia, rather than a required defining feature.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: dental dysplasia is a defining ectodermal component; microdontia, fused teeth and abnormal spacing occurred in 2/2 patients. Teeth belong to gastrointestinal.

basis: Joubert CNS malformation with developmental impairment; the ocular-defect parent and retinal disease or optic pallor in 1/2 support a defining ocular component.

decisions.ocular: primary: explicitly classified as Joubert syndrome with ocular defect; pigmentary retinopathy and optic disc pallor each occur in 1/2 reported patients.

basis: Motor neuropathy with defining persistent vocal cord paresis and impaired laryngeal function; distal muscle wasting is secondary to motor denervation.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: distal weakness and wasting result from motor denervation; the evidence does not establish direct muscle disease independent of the neuropathy.
